elements.name: sl:slot
elements.description: Content for a named slot of the enclosing component. Inside a component template: where that content goes, with this element's body as the fallback.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: The named slot to fill, e.g. `icon-start`. Omit it for the default slot.

elements.name: sl:accordion
elements.description: A stack of sections, each with a heading that shows or hides its content. Built on the browser's `details` element, so it needs no JavaScript: the keyboard, the open state, and find-in-page opening a section that holds a match all come from the browser. Holds `sl:accordion-item`s, each with a `sl:accordion-trigger` and a `sl:accordion-content`.

attributes.name: type
attributes.description: `single`: opening a section closes the one that was open (the items share a `details` `name`). `multiple`: sections open and close on their own.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: The group name the items of a `single` accordion share. Must be unique on the page. Without it, each render generates one (`sl-accordion-` and eight random characters).

elements.name: sl:accordion-content
elements.description: The content of a `sl:accordion-item`, shown while it is open. Find-in-page searches it while it is closed, and opens the section on a match.

elements.name: sl:accordion-item
elements.description: One section of a `sl:accordion`: a `details` element holding a `sl:accordion-trigger` (first) and a `sl:accordion-content`.

attributes.name: open
attributes.description: Render the section open. In a `single` accordion only the first open section stays open.

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description: The section cannot be opened or closed: its trigger is out of the tab order and ignores the pointer, and a closed disabled section renders no content, so find-in-page cannot open it.

elements.name: sl:accordion-trigger
elements.description: The heading of a `sl:accordion-item`, which opens and closes it: the `details` element's `summary`, so it must be the item's first child. Its text is a heading inside the `summary`, and a chevron follows it.

attributes.name: level
attributes.description: Heading level of the text (`role="heading"` and `aria-level`), as shadcn/ui's trigger sits in an `h3`. Pick the level that fits the page's outline.

elements.name: sl:alert
elements.description: A callout for a message the user should notice: an optional `sl:icon`, then `sl:alert-title` and `sl:alert-description`. It is not announced by itself; add `role="alert"` when it appears after the page loaded, such as in an htmx response.

elements.name: sl:alert-description
elements.description: The body of an alert, inside `sl:alert`: text, paragraphs or a list.

elements.name: sl:alert-dialog
elements.description: A modal dialog that interrupts the user with something important and waits for an answer, such as a confirmation before deleting. Built on the native `dialog` element with `role="alertdialog"`: a click outside does not close it, Escape does. Build it from `sl:alert-dialog-header` (with an optional `sl:alert-dialog-media`, `sl:alert-dialog-title` and `sl:alert-dialog-description`) and `sl:alert-dialog-footer` holding `sl:alert-dialog-cancel`, which takes the focus when the dialog opens, and the action, a `sl:button`. A button opens it with `commandfor` set to its `id` and `command="show-modal"`; an htmx response closes it with the `sl-dialog-close` event.

attributes.name: id
attributes.description: The dialog's id, which the button that opens it points at with `commandfor`. The title and description ids derive from it.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description: Size of the dialog. `sm` is narrower, with the header centred and the footer's two buttons side by side.

attributes.name: open
attributes.description: Open the dialog as soon as it is on the page, for a dialog the server renders in answer to a request (an htmx swap). Needs Alpine.

elements.name: sl:alert-dialog-cancel
elements.description: The button that closes a `sl:alert-dialog` without doing anything, in its `sl:alert-dialog-footer`. It takes the focus when the dialog opens, so Enter never confirms by accident. Its text defaults to "Cancel" (`sl.alert-dialog.cancel`); content of its own replaces it. Any other attribute passes through to the `sl:button`.

attributes.name: variant
attributes.description: Visual style of the button, as on `sl:button`.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description: Size of the button, as on `sl:button`.

elements.name: sl:alert-dialog-description
elements.description: Supporting text below a `sl:alert-dialog-title`, which describes the dialog (`aria-describedby`): what happens, and whether it can be undone. Its id derives from the dialog's (`delete-account-description`).

elements.name: sl:alert-dialog-footer
elements.description: The bottom of a `sl:alert-dialog`, for `sl:alert-dialog-cancel` and the action: side by side at the end on a wide screen, stacked with the first one at the bottom on a narrow one, and two equal columns in a small dialog.

elements.name: sl:alert-dialog-header
elements.description: The top of a `sl:alert-dialog`: an optional `sl:alert-dialog-media`, a `sl:alert-dialog-title` and an optional `sl:alert-dialog-description`. Centred on a narrow screen and in a small dialog.

elements.name: sl:alert-dialog-media
elements.description: An icon (or an image) at the start of a `sl:alert-dialog-header`, on a muted square: above the title, or beside title and description in a wide dialog.

attributes.name: variant
attributes.description: Colour of the square and its icon: `destructive` for a dialog that confirms deleting something.

elements.name: sl:alert-dialog-title
elements.description: The title of a `sl:alert-dialog`, inside `sl:alert-dialog-header`: a heading that names the dialog (`aria-labelledby`). Its id derives from the dialog's (`delete-account-title`).

attributes.name: level
attributes.description: Heading level (`role="heading"` and `aria-level`). A dialog starts an outline of its own, so the default, 2, rarely needs changing.

elements.name: sl:alert-title
elements.description: The title of an alert, inside `sl:alert`.

attributes.name: level
attributes.description: Heading level. With it the title is a heading (`role="heading"` and `aria-level`) that screen reader users can jump to; without it, plain text, as in shadcn/ui.

elements.name: sl:attachment
elements.description: A file or an image attached to something: a message, a form, a record. Holds an `sl:attachment-media`, an `sl:attachment-content` (title and description), optional `sl:attachment-actions` and an optional `sl:attachment-trigger` that makes the whole card open a link or a dialog. Purely presentational: the server renders its state. Say the state in the description too ("Uploading · 64%", "Upload failed"), so it is not told by colour alone.

attributes.name: state
attributes.description: Where the file is in its upload: `idle` (picked, not sent yet) draws a dashed border, `uploading` and `processing` shimmer the title and mark the attachment busy (`aria-busy`), `error` turns it destructive. `done` is a file that is there.

attributes.name: orientation
attributes.description: `vertical` puts the media above the content, for an image.

attributes.name: full-width
attributes.description: Fill the width of the container, for a list of attachments (shadcn's `w-full` class). Without it the attachment is as wide as its content.

elements.name: sl:attachment-action
elements.description: A button in `sl:attachment-actions`, to remove, retry or download the file: a `sl:button`, ghost and an extra small icon by default. Give it an `aria-label` that names the file ("Remove report.pdf"). Any other attribute passes through to the `sl:button` (`href`, `type`, `disabled`, `hx-*`). Requires `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` when `size` is `icon`, `icon-xs`, `icon-sm` or `icon-lg`.

attributes.name: variant
attributes.description: Visual style of the button, as on `sl:button`.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description: Size of the button, as on `sl:button`. The `icon` sizes are square, for a button that holds only an icon, and need an `aria-label`.

attributes.name: as
attributes.description: Element to render: a `button`, or an anchor (`a`) to download or open the file.

elements.name: sl:attachment-actions
elements.description: The `sl:attachment-action`s of an attachment, at its end; in a vertical attachment, over the top corner of the media. They sit above an `sl:attachment-trigger`, so they stay clickable.

elements.name: sl:attachment-content
elements.description: The text of an `sl:attachment`: its `sl:attachment-title` and `sl:attachment-description`. Takes the space the media and the actions leave.

elements.name: sl:attachment-description
elements.description: What else to know about an attachment, below its title: the file type and size, or its state ("Uploading · 64%", "Upload failed. Try again."). Cut off with an ellipsis when it does not fit.

elements.name: sl:attachment-group
elements.description: A row of `sl:attachment`s that scrolls sideways when they do not fit, snapping to each attachment, its edges fading out. Keyboard users reach attachments off screen by tabbing to their actions or triggers; for attachments without any, give the group a `label`.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Accessible name of the group. With it the group is a named group (`role="group"`) that takes keyboard focus, so the arrow keys scroll it: for a row of attachments that have no actions or trigger.

elements.name: sl:attachment-media
elements.description: The icon or image of an `sl:attachment`: an icon (or an `sl:spinner` while it uploads) on a muted square, or an `<img>` that fills it.

attributes.name: variant
attributes.description: `icon` centres an icon on a muted square; `image` crops an `<img>` to fill the square, dimmed while the attachment uploads, is processed or failed.

elements.name: sl:attachment-title
elements.description: The name of an attachment, usually its file name, in `sl:attachment-content`. Cut off with an ellipsis when it does not fit; shimmers while the attachment uploads or is processed, unless the user asks for reduced motion.

elements.name: sl:attachment-trigger
elements.description: Makes a whole `sl:attachment` clickable: a button (to open an `sl:dialog` with `commandfor` and `command="show-modal"`) or, with `as="a"`, a link that covers the card behind its actions. It has no text of its own, so it needs an `aria-label` that says what it does ("Open report.pdf"). Put it last in the attachment. Requires `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.

attributes.name: as
attributes.description: Element to render: a `button`, or an anchor (`a`) to open the file.

elements.name: sl:avatar
elements.description: A picture of a person: an `sl:avatar-image`, and an `sl:avatar-fallback` (initials) shown instead while the image has no `src`, is loading or fails to load. Decorative unless it has a `label`, as an avatar usually sits next to the person's name.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: The person's name, for an avatar with no name next to it. It is then announced as an image with that name; without it the avatar is hidden from assistive technology.

elements.name: sl:avatar-fallback
elements.description: What `sl:avatar` shows when its image has no `src`, while it loads and when it fails to load: usually the person's initials, or an `sl:icon`.

elements.name: sl:avatar-image
elements.description: The picture inside `sl:avatar`. Pass `src` or `th:src`; when it is empty or null, while the picture loads, and when it fails to load (marked by Shadleaf's script), the image is hidden and the `sl:avatar-fallback` shows instead. The avatar's `label` names it, so the image itself has an empty `alt`.

elements.name: sl:badge
elements.description: A small label for a status, a count or a category; with `as="a"`, a link that looks the same. Every attribute that is not a prop passes through; `class` is appended to `badge`.

attributes.name: as
attributes.description: Element to render: a `span`, or an anchor (`a`) for a badge that links somewhere. Only a linked badge reacts to hover.

elements.name: sl:breadcrumb
elements.description: The trail of pages above the one shown now, in a `nav` named "Breadcrumb" (the message `sl.breadcrumb.label`; an `aria-label` replaces it). Holds a `sl:breadcrumb-list` with `sl:breadcrumb-item`s, each a `sl:breadcrumb-link` or, last, the `sl:breadcrumb-page`, with a `sl:breadcrumb-separator` between them.

elements.name: sl:breadcrumb-ellipsis
elements.description: Stands for the levels a long trail leaves out. Without content it is an ellipsis, read as "More levels" (the message `sl.breadcrumb.more`). With content, the `sl:dropdown-menu-item`s of those levels (`as="a"`), it is a ghost icon button named "Show more levels" (`sl.breadcrumb.more.trigger`; an `aria-label` replaces it) that opens a `sl:dropdown-menu` of them; any other attribute then goes to the button.

attributes.name: id
attributes.description: With content: the menu's id, `breadcrumb-more` when not set (the button's is `<id>-trigger`); give a second breadcrumb on the page another one. Without content: the ellipsis's own id.

elements.name: sl:breadcrumb-item
elements.description: One level of a `sl:breadcrumb-list`: a `sl:breadcrumb-link`, the `sl:breadcrumb-page`, a `sl:breadcrumb-ellipsis`, or plain text for a level that has no page of its own.

elements.name: sl:breadcrumb-link
elements.description: A link to a level above the page shown now. Give it an `href` or `th:href`. A level without a page of its own is plain text in its `sl:breadcrumb-item` instead.

elements.name: sl:breadcrumb-list
elements.description: The ordered list of a `sl:breadcrumb`: its items and the separators between them, on one line that wraps when there is no room.

elements.name: sl:breadcrumb-page
elements.description: The page shown now, last in the trail: text in the foreground colour, marked `aria-current="page"`. Not a link.

elements.name: sl:breadcrumb-separator
elements.description: The mark between two items of a `sl:breadcrumb-list`: a chevron that points the other way on a right-to-left page. Content of its own (another icon, a slash) replaces it; that content is not turned around. Decorative: screen readers skip it, so the list holds only the levels.

elements.name: sl:button
elements.description: A button, or with `as="a"` an anchor that looks the same. Every attribute that is not a prop (`hx-*`, `x-*`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, `href`) passes through; `class` is appended to `button`. Requires `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` when `size` is `icon`, `icon-xs`, `icon-sm` or `icon-lg`.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description: Size of the button. The `icon` sizes are square, for a button that holds only an icon, and need an `aria-label`.

attributes.name: as
attributes.description: Element to render: a `button`, an anchor (`a`) for navigation, or a `label` for a visually hidden control (`for`), as `sl:file-upload`'s Browse button for its file input. A label takes no focus and no `disabled`: the control does.

attributes.name: type
attributes.description: Submit behaviour. Defaults to `button`, unlike HTML, so a button in a form never submits by accident.

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description: Disable the button. A disabled anchor loses its `href` and leaves the tab order.

attributes.name: loading
attributes.description: Show a spinner, announce the busy state and disable the button.

elements.name: sl:calendar
elements.description: A month calendar to pick a date or a range of dates, drawn over native date inputs: the inputs are its value, so `th:field` binds it and the form submits ISO dates (`2026-10-23`). Without content, it renders one date input itself, which takes every attribute that is not a prop except `class` (`th:field`, `name`, `required`, `min`, `max`), and in a `sl:field` the field's `th:field`, id and `aria-describedby`. For a range, give it two `sl:input type="date"`s as content, the start and the end; its attributes then go to the calendar. `slCalendar` hides the inputs and draws the month; without JavaScript the inputs show as they are.

attributes.name: caption-layout
attributes.description: The month's caption: its name, or selects for the month and year, the month, or the year.

attributes.name: number-of-months
attributes.description: How many months show side by side (stacked on a narrow screen).

attributes.name: show-outside-days
attributes.description: Show the days of the previous and next month that fill the first and last week.

attributes.name: show-week-number
attributes.description: Show the week numbers, counted as the page's locale counts them (ISO weeks in most of Europe).

attributes.name: week-starts-on
attributes.description: The first day of the week: 0 is Sunday, 1 Monday, up to 6. By default the page's locale decides.

attributes.name: default-month
attributes.description: The month shown first, as `2026-10`. By default the month of the chosen date (or of the start of the range), or else the current month.

attributes.name: start-month
attributes.description: The first month the calendar navigates to, as `2026-01`; also the first year of the year select. By default the month of the inputs' `min`, or else 100 years ago.

attributes.name: end-month
attributes.description: The last month the calendar navigates to, as `2026-12`; also the last year of the year select. By default the month of the inputs' `max`, or else 10 years from now.

attributes.name: disabled-dates
attributes.description: Days that cannot be picked, comma-separated: a date (`2026-12-25`), a range (`2026-12-24..2026-12-31`) or a day of the week (`sat`, `sun`). The inputs' `min` and `max` disable the days outside them too. Only the calendar knows: check the date on the server as well.

elements.name: sl:card
elements.description: A container for related content and actions. Build it from its parts, in any order and number: `sl:card-header` (holding `sl:card-title`, `sl:card-description` and `sl:card-action`), `sl:card-content` and `sl:card-footer`. An `img` as the first or last child runs to the card's edges.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description: Spacing inside the card and between its parts.

elements.name: sl:card-action
elements.description: An action in the top end corner of a card, such as a button or a badge, inside `sl:card-header`.

elements.name: sl:card-content
elements.description: The body of a card.

elements.name: sl:card-description
elements.description: Supporting text below a `sl:card-title`, inside `sl:card-header`.

elements.name: sl:card-footer
elements.description: The bottom of a card, for actions or a summary.

attributes.name: border
attributes.description: A dividing line above the footer, with matching spacing.

elements.name: sl:card-header
elements.description: The top of a card: a `sl:card-title`, an optional `sl:card-description` below it, and an optional `sl:card-action` beside both.

attributes.name: border
attributes.description: A dividing line below the header, with matching spacing.

elements.name: sl:card-title
elements.description: The title of a card, inside `sl:card-header`.

attributes.name: level
attributes.description: Heading level. With it the title is a heading (`role="heading"` and `aria-level`) that screen reader users can jump to; without it, plain text. Pick the level that fits the page's outline.

elements.name: sl:chart
elements.description: A chart drawn by Recharts in the browser, as shadcn's: bars, lines and areas over a category or time axis, with a grid, axes, a tooltip and a legend. Pass the rows in `th:data` and put the parts inside, in the order Recharts draws them: `sl:chart-grid`, `sl:chart-x-axis`, `sl:chart-y-axis`, `sl:chart-tooltip`, `sl:chart-legend`, then one `sl:chart-bar`, `sl:chart-line` or `sl:chart-area` per series (only bars give a bar chart, a mix a composed chart). Needs JavaScript: without it the chart's skeleton stays. The chart is 16:9; for a fixed height, give it one in your CSS with `aspect-ratio: auto`. Every attribute that is not a prop passes through to the element.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: The chart's accessible name, such as its title: what a screen reader announces when the chart takes the focus.

attributes.name: margin
attributes.description: Space in pixels left and right of the plot, so the first and last tick labels fit (shadcn's line and area charts use 12).

attributes.name: time-zone
attributes.description: The time zone (an IANA id such as `Europe/Brussels`) instants in the data are shown in: `Instant`, `OffsetDateTime` and `ZonedDateTime`. Defaults to the request's (Spring's `LocaleContextHolder`). A `LocalDate` or `LocalDateTime` is shown as written, in any zone.

attributes.name: th:data
attributes.description: The rows: a list (or a Spring Data `Page`) of objects, records or maps, one per category or point in time. Each row holds the category (`month`) and a number per series (`desktop`, `mobile`). Serialised with Jackson: dates as ISO strings, which the named date formats read by their Java type.

elements.name: sl:chart-area
elements.description: One series of a `sl:chart`, drawn as a filled area under a line through the rows. Draws no element of its own on the page: the chart reads it.

attributes.name: key
attributes.description: The property of the rows that holds this series' numbers (`desktop`): letters, digits, `_` and `-`, as it also names the colour property `--color-<key>`.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: The series' name in the tooltip and the legend, typically a message (`th:label="#{visitors.desktop}"`). Defaults to the key.

attributes.name: color
attributes.description: Its colour, any CSS colour (`var(--chart-3)`, `#2563eb`). Defaults to the chart tokens in turn: the first series `var(--chart-1)`, the second `var(--chart-2)`, and so on (after the fifth, again from the first).

attributes.name: color-dark
attributes.description: A different colour in the dark theme; `color` is then the light one (the two go into `light-dark()`).

attributes.name: curve
attributes.description: How the line runs between the points: smooth (`natural`, `monotone`), straight (`linear`) or in steps.

attributes.name: stack
attributes.description: Stack this series on the others with the same `stack` id (any name, such as `a`).

attributes.name: fill-opacity
attributes.description: The opacity of the fill, from 0 to 1.

elements.name: sl:chart-bar
elements.description: One series of a `sl:chart`, drawn as bars: one per row. Draws no element of its own on the page: the chart reads it.

attributes.name: key
attributes.description: The property of the rows that holds this series' numbers (`desktop`): letters, digits, `_` and `-`, as it also names the colour property `--color-<key>`.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: The series' name in the tooltip and the legend, typically a message (`th:label="#{visitors.desktop}"`). Defaults to the key.

attributes.name: color
attributes.description: Its colour, any CSS colour (`var(--chart-3)`, `#2563eb`). Defaults to the chart tokens in turn: the first series `var(--chart-1)`, the second `var(--chart-2)`, and so on (after the fifth, again from the first).

attributes.name: color-dark
attributes.description: A different colour in the dark theme; `color` is then the light one (the two go into `light-dark()`).

attributes.name: radius
attributes.description: The bars' corner radius in pixels: `4` for every corner, or four numbers (top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left), as `4,4,0,0` for the top bar of a stack.

attributes.name: stack
attributes.description: Stack this series on the others with the same `stack` id (any name, such as `a`) instead of drawing them side by side.

elements.name: sl:chart-grid
elements.description: The grid lines behind a `sl:chart`'s plot. Draws no element of its own on the page: the chart reads it.

attributes.name: vertical
attributes.description: Vertical lines too, one per category.

attributes.name: horizontal
attributes.description: Horizontal lines, one per value tick.

elements.name: sl:chart-legend
elements.description: The legend of a `sl:chart`: every series' label with its colour. Draws no element of its own on the page: the chart reads it.

attributes.name: vertical-align
attributes.description: Below the plot, or above it.

elements.name: sl:chart-line
elements.description: One series of a `sl:chart`, drawn as a line through the rows. Draws no element of its own on the page: the chart reads it.

attributes.name: key
attributes.description: The property of the rows that holds this series' numbers (`desktop`): letters, digits, `_` and `-`, as it also names the colour property `--color-<key>`.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: The series' name in the tooltip and the legend, typically a message (`th:label="#{visitors.desktop}"`). Defaults to the key.

attributes.name: color
attributes.description: Its colour, any CSS colour (`var(--chart-3)`, `#2563eb`). Defaults to the chart tokens in turn: the first series `var(--chart-1)`, the second `var(--chart-2)`, and so on (after the fifth, again from the first).

attributes.name: color-dark
attributes.description: A different colour in the dark theme; `color` is then the light one (the two go into `light-dark()`).

attributes.name: curve
attributes.description: How the line runs between the points: smooth (`monotone`, `natural`), straight (`linear`) or in steps.

elements.name: sl:chart-tooltip
elements.description: The tooltip of a `sl:chart`: on hover, or with the arrow keys once the chart has the focus, it shows the category and every series' label and value. Draws no element of its own on the page: the chart reads it.

attributes.name: indicator
attributes.description: The mark before each series' label, in its colour.

attributes.name: cursor
attributes.description: Highlight the hovered category (a band behind bars, a line over lines and areas).

attributes.name: hide-label
attributes.description: Leave out the label at the top (the category).

attributes.name: hide-indicator
attributes.description: Leave out the marks before the series' labels.

attributes.name: label-key
attributes.description: The property of the rows to take the label from instead of the axis category: a series key gives that series' label, any other property its value in the hovered row, such as a date the server formatted.

attributes.name: label-format
attributes.description: How the label is written, as the ticks of `sl:chart-x-axis` (`month`, `date`, ...). Without one, as it is.

attributes.name: value-format
attributes.description: How the values are written: `number` in the page's language, or `currency`, `percent`, ...

attributes.name: currency
attributes.description: The ISO 4217 code (`EUR`) for a `currency` format.

elements.name: sl:chart-x-axis
elements.description: The category or time axis of a `sl:chart`, along the bottom: its ticks are the values of `key` in the rows, without tick or axis lines (as shadcn's). Under `dir="rtl"` it runs from right to left. Draws no element of its own on the page: the chart reads it.

attributes.name: key
attributes.description: The property of the rows that holds the category (`month`) or the date.

attributes.name: format
attributes.description: How the ticks are written, with `Intl` in the page's language. Numbers: `number`, `integer`, `compact` (1.2K), `percent` (0.25 is 25%), `currency` (with `currency`). Dates: `day` (Apr 1), `month-short` (Apr), `month` (April), `month-year` (Apr 2024), `date`, `time`. Without one, the values as they are.

attributes.name: tick-margin
attributes.description: Space in pixels between the ticks and the plot.

attributes.name: min-tick-gap
attributes.description: The least space in pixels between two ticks; Recharts leaves out ticks that would come closer, as on a long time axis.

elements.name: sl:chart-y-axis
elements.description: The value axis of a `sl:chart`, at the start side (the left, or the right under `dir="rtl"`), without tick or axis lines. shadcn's charts often leave it out and show the values in the tooltip. Draws no element of its own on the page: the chart reads it.

attributes.name: format
attributes.description: How the ticks are written, as on `sl:chart-x-axis`: `compact` (1.2K) and `currency` suit a value axis.

attributes.name: tick-margin
attributes.description: Space in pixels between the ticks and the plot.

attributes.name: tick-count
attributes.description: How many ticks Recharts aims for.

elements.name: sl:checkbox
elements.description: A checkbox: the browser's own, styled. Every attribute that is not a prop (`th:field`, `name`, `value`, `checked`, `required`) passes through to the `input`, except `class`, which goes to the wrapper that holds the check mark. With `th:field`, Spring numbers the id (`terms1`), so put the checkbox inside its label, in a `sl:field` (which gives it the field's name as id), or give it an explicit `id`; the checkbox is marked `aria-invalid` when its field has errors. A checkbox in the indeterminate state (neither checked nor unchecked: some of a group selected) shows a minus.

attributes.name: indeterminate
attributes.description: Start in the indeterminate state. HTML has no attribute for it, only the DOM property `indeterminate`: this renders `data-indeterminate`, from which Shadleaf's script sets the property when the page loads (or htmx swaps the checkbox in). A click clears it, as it does on every checkbox. A script can set the property on any checkbox; the minus follows it.

elements.name: sl:collapsible
elements.description: Content that a button shows and hides. Built on the browser's `details` element, so it needs no JavaScript. Holds a `sl:collapsible-trigger` (first) and a `sl:collapsible-content`.

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description: It cannot be opened or closed: its trigger is out of the tab order and ignores the pointer, and closed it renders no content, so find-in-page cannot open it.

elements.name: sl:collapsible-content
elements.description: The content of a `sl:collapsible`, shown while it is open. Find-in-page searches it while it is closed, and opens it on a match.

elements.name: sl:collapsible-trigger
elements.description: What the user clicks to open and close a `sl:collapsible`: its `details` element's `summary`, so it must come first. Plain text by default; `variant` or `size` draws it as a `sl:button`. Requires `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` when `size` is `icon`, `icon-xs`, `icon-sm` or `icon-lg`.

attributes.name: variant
attributes.description: Draw the trigger as a button of this variant, as on `sl:button`.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description: Draw the trigger as a button of this size, as on `sl:button`. The `icon` sizes need an `aria-label`.

elements.name: sl:combobox
elements.description: A text input that filters a list of options as you type: shadcn/ui's combobox. Like `sl:select`, it is a real `select` with `sl:combobox-item`, `sl:combobox-group` and `sl:combobox-separator` as content, so `th:field` binds it (a collection with `multiple`) and the form submits it. Once Alpine runs, `slCombobox` hides the select and puts an input and a list box in its place; without it, the select is drawn like `sl:native-select`. Every attribute that is not a prop passes through to the `select`, except `class`, which goes to the wrapper around it. In a `sl:field`, it takes the field's `th:field`, id and `aria-describedby`.

attributes.name: placeholder
attributes.description: The input's text while nothing is chosen. For a single value also the text of a first option with an empty value, hidden from the list: a required combobox with it chosen is invalid.

attributes.name: multiple
attributes.description: Choose any number of options, shown as chips before the input. The select is a `select multiple`, so `th:field` binds a collection.

attributes.name: show-clear
attributes.description: A button that clears the choice, in place of the chevron while there is one.

attributes.name: show-trigger
attributes.description: The chevron button that opens and closes the list. A multiple combobox has none.

attributes.name: auto-highlight
attributes.description: Highlight the first match while typing, so Enter chooses it.

attributes.name: empty
attributes.description: The text shown when no option matches. By default "No items found."

attributes.name: search-url
attributes.description: Ask the server for the options as you type: a `GET` to this URL with the text as `q`, answered with the HTML of `sl:combobox-item`s (and groups and separators), which replace the options that are not chosen. Needs JavaScript; without it, only the options in the page can be chosen.

elements.name: sl:combobox-group
elements.description: A group of `sl:combobox-item`s under a heading: an `optgroup`. The list hides the heading while none of its items match.

elements.name: sl:combobox-item
elements.description: An option in a `sl:combobox`: an `option`. `value` (or `th:value`) and `disabled` pass through; `th:field` on the combobox marks the bound one. The list shows its content, which may start with an icon, with a check mark while it is chosen; the input, the chips and the filter use its text, which is all an older browser keeps of it.

elements.name: sl:combobox-separator
elements.description: A line between items or groups of a `sl:combobox`: an `hr`. The list hides it while you type.

elements.name: sl:date-picker
elements.description: A button showing the chosen date that opens a `sl:calendar` in a popover: shadcn/ui's date picker, made of its popover and calendar, as one component. Its value lives in the calendar's date inputs, so `th:field` binds it and the form submits ISO dates. Every attribute that is not a prop goes to the `sl:calendar` inside, except `class`, which stays on the date picker: the calendar's props (`caption-layout`, `number-of-months`, `disabled-dates`, ...) and, for a single date, the attributes of its input (`th:field`, `name`, `required`, `min`, `max`). In a `sl:field`, the input takes the field's `th:field`, id and `aria-describedby`, and the button is named by the field's label. For a range, give it two `sl:input type="date"`s as content, the start and the end, and an `aria-label`. A pick closes the popover; for a range the second pick does. Needs JavaScript (`slDatePicker`).

attributes.name: placeholder
attributes.description: The button's text while no date is chosen. By default "Pick a date".

attributes.name: format
attributes.description: How the button shows the date, in the page's locale: as `Intl.DateTimeFormat`'s `dateStyle` and Java's `FormatStyle` (`10/23/26`, `Oct 23, 2026`, `October 23, 2026`, `Friday, October 23, 2026`).

attributes.name: popover-id
attributes.description: The popover's id, which the button points at with `popovertarget`. By default a generated one (`sl-date-picker-` and eight random characters).

elements.name: sl:dialog
elements.description: A modal dialog on the native `dialog` element: the page behind it is inert, Escape and a click outside close it, and focus returns to where it came from. Build it from `sl:dialog-header` (holding `sl:dialog-title` and `sl:dialog-description`), your content and `sl:dialog-footer`. A button opens it with `commandfor` set to the dialog's `id` and `command="show-modal"`, and closes it with `command="close"`; an htmx response closes it with the `sl-dialog-close` event.

attributes.name: id
attributes.description: The dialog's id, which the buttons that open and close it point at with `commandfor`. The title and description ids derive from it.

attributes.name: open
attributes.description: Open the dialog as soon as it is on the page, for a dialog the server renders in answer to a request (an htmx swap, or a page shown after a redirect). Needs Alpine.

attributes.name: show-close-button
attributes.description: A close button (an x) in the corner.

elements.name: sl:dialog-body
elements.description: The content of a `sl:dialog` between its header and footer, which scrolls by itself so the header and footer stay in view. Its content has the id `<id>-body` (`edit-body`), the target for htmx: a request from outside that targets it opens the dialog at once and shows a spinner until the answer is swapped in; closing aborts a request still running. Left empty, it is emptied again when the dialog closes, so it never shows the previous content. When a request fails, the error shows in the dialog, or, for the request that opened it, as a toast (see `load-error`). Needs Alpine.

attributes.name: load-error
attributes.description: What happens when the request that opened the dialog fails: `toast` closes it and shows the error as a toast (shown in the dialog when the page has no `sl:toaster`); `inline` keeps it open with the error in it. A failed request from inside (a form) always shows the error in the dialog, so nothing typed is lost.

elements.name: sl:dialog-description
elements.description: Supporting text below a `sl:dialog-title`, which describes the dialog (`aria-describedby`). Its id derives from the dialog's (`edit-profile-description`).

elements.name: sl:dialog-footer
elements.description: The bottom of a `sl:dialog`, for its actions: side by side at the end on a wide screen, stacked with the first one at the bottom on a narrow one.

attributes.name: show-close-button
attributes.description: An outline "Close" button after the other actions.

elements.name: sl:dialog-header
elements.description: The top of a `sl:dialog`: a `sl:dialog-title` and an optional `sl:dialog-description` below it.

elements.name: sl:dialog-title
elements.description: The title of a `sl:dialog`, inside `sl:dialog-header`: a heading that names the dialog (`aria-labelledby`). Its id derives from the dialog's (`edit-profile-title`).

attributes.name: level
attributes.description: Heading level (`role="heading"` and `aria-level`). A dialog starts an outline of its own, so the default, 2, rarely needs changing.

elements.name: sl:dropdown-menu
elements.description: A menu of actions or links that opens from a button, on the browser's Popover API: it sits above the page, and Escape or a click outside closes it. Holds a `sl:dropdown-menu-trigger` and a `sl:dropdown-menu-content` with the items. Renders no element of its own. Needs Alpine for the arrow keys, typeahead and closing after an item is chosen.

attributes.name: id
attributes.description: The menu's id, which the trigger points at with `popovertarget`. Any other button can open it that way too.

elements.name: sl:dropdown-menu-checkbox-item
elements.description: An item in a `sl:dropdown-menu-content` that shows an on/off state with a check mark (`role="menuitemcheckbox"`), such as a filter or a view setting. The state comes from the server: choosing the item does what its attributes say (a link to `?archived=true`, an `hx-post`), and the page or fragment that comes back shows the new state. Give it its text as content (`[[${...}]]`), not with `th:text`, which would replace the check mark too. Otherwise as `sl:dropdown-menu-item`.

attributes.name: as
attributes.description: Element to render: a `button`, or an anchor (`a`).

attributes.name: type
attributes.description: Submit behaviour of a button item.

attributes.name: inset
attributes.description: Indent the item to line up with items that start with an icon.

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description: Disable the item. The arrow keys skip it.

elements.name: sl:dropdown-menu-content
elements.description: The menu itself, inside `sl:dropdown-menu`: a popover next to its trigger, in the top layer, holding the items, labels, groups and separators. It flips to the other side when there is no room.

attributes.name: side
attributes.description: The side of the trigger it opens on. `right` and `left` are the end and the start of a line: on a right-to-left page a `right` menu opens on the left.

attributes.name: align
attributes.description: How it lines up with the trigger along that side: `start` lines up the start edges.

elements.name: sl:dropdown-menu-group
elements.description: Items that belong together in a `sl:dropdown-menu-content` (`role="group"`), usually between separators or under a label.

elements.name: sl:dropdown-menu-item
elements.description: An action in a `sl:dropdown-menu-content`: a button, or with `as="a"` a link. Every attribute that is not a prop (`hx-*`, `href`, `commandfor`, `form`) passes through, and the menu closes once the item is chosen.

attributes.name: as
attributes.description: Element to render: a `button`, or an anchor (`a`) for navigation.

attributes.name: variant
attributes.description: `destructive` for an item that deletes something.

attributes.name: type
attributes.description: Submit behaviour of a button item. Defaults to `button`; `submit` submits the form it is in (or names with `form`).

attributes.name: inset
attributes.description: Indent the item to line up with items that start with an icon.

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description: Disable the item. The arrow keys skip it; a disabled link loses its `href`.

elements.name: sl:dropdown-menu-label
elements.description: A heading for the items below it in a `sl:dropdown-menu-content`. It cannot be chosen, and the arrow keys pass it by.

attributes.name: inset
attributes.description: Indent the label to line up with items that start with an icon.

elements.name: sl:dropdown-menu-radio-group
elements.description: A set of `sl:dropdown-menu-radio-item`s in a menu, one of which is chosen (`role="group"`). Name it with `aria-label` when a label above it does not make the choice clear.

elements.name: sl:dropdown-menu-radio-item
elements.description: One of a set of choices in a `sl:dropdown-menu-radio-group`, with a check mark on the chosen one (`role="menuitemradio"`), such as the sort order of a list. The server marks the chosen one `checked`: each item is a link (`?sort=name`) or a request, and the page or fragment that comes back shows the new choice. Give it its text as content (`[[${...}]]`), not with `th:text`, which would replace the check mark too. Otherwise as `sl:dropdown-menu-item`.

attributes.name: checked
attributes.description: Whether this is the chosen item (`aria-checked`).

attributes.name: as
attributes.description: Element to render: a `button`, or an anchor (`a`).

attributes.name: type
attributes.description: Submit behaviour of a button item.

attributes.name: inset
attributes.description: Indent the item to line up with items that start with an icon.

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description: Disable the item. The arrow keys skip it.

elements.name: sl:dropdown-menu-separator
elements.description: A line between groups of items in a `sl:dropdown-menu-content` (`role="separator"`).

elements.name: sl:dropdown-menu-shortcut
elements.description: A keyboard shortcut at the end of a `sl:dropdown-menu-item`, such as `⌘S`. It only shows the shortcut; the application handles the keys. Typeahead ignores it.

elements.name: sl:dropdown-menu-trigger
elements.description: What opens and closes a `sl:dropdown-menu`: by default a `sl:button`, or with `as` a sidebar part (shadcn's `<DropdownMenuTrigger asChild>`). It renders that part with `popovertarget` set to the menu, which it names. Arrow down opens the menu on its first item, arrow up on its last. Its `icon-start` and `icon-end` slots go to the part's; any other attribute passes through to it.

attributes.name: as
attributes.description: The part to render: a `sl:button`, a `sl:sidebar-menu-button` (a team switcher or user menu in a `sl:sidebar-menu-item`), or a `sl:sidebar-menu-action` (a "More" beside a menu button, which needs an `aria-label`).

attributes.name: variant
attributes.description: Visual style, as on `sl:button`, or `default` and `outline` as on `sl:sidebar-menu-button`. Not for a sidebar menu action.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description: Size, as on `sl:button` (the `icon` sizes need an `aria-label`), or `sm`, `default` and `lg` as on `sl:sidebar-menu-button`. Not for a sidebar menu action.

attributes.name: tooltip
attributes.description: With `as="sidebar-menu-button"`: the label shown beside it while the sidebar is collapsed to icons, as on `sl:sidebar-menu-button`. Never shown while the menu is open.

attributes.name: show-on-hover
attributes.description: With `as="sidebar-menu-action"`: from 768 px, show it only while the pointer is over its item, the focus is in it, or the menu is open.

elements.name: sl:empty
elements.description: An empty state: what a list, a table, a search or a page shows when there is nothing to show yet. Holds an `sl:empty-header` (media, title and description) and an optional `sl:empty-content` with what to do next, centred in the space it is given.

attributes.name: border
attributes.description: A dashed line around the empty state, to mark out the area (shadcn's `border border-dashed` classes).

elements.name: sl:empty-content
elements.description: What to do next in an `sl:empty`, below its header: a button, a search field, a link.

elements.name: sl:empty-description
elements.description: The text below the title of an `sl:empty`. Links in it are underlined.

elements.name: sl:empty-header
elements.description: The top of an `sl:empty`: an optional `sl:empty-media`, an `sl:empty-title` and an `sl:empty-description`, stacked and centred.

elements.name: sl:empty-media
elements.description: An icon, an avatar or an image above the title of an `sl:empty`, inside `sl:empty-header`.

attributes.name: variant
attributes.description: `icon` puts an icon on a muted square; `default` shows the content as it is, e.g. an avatar.

elements.name: sl:empty-title
elements.description: The title of an `sl:empty`, inside `sl:empty-header`.

attributes.name: level
attributes.description: Heading level. With it the title is a heading (`role="heading"` and `aria-level`) that screen reader users can jump to; without it, plain text. Pick the level that fits the page's outline.

elements.name: sl:field
elements.description: A form field: a `sl:field-label`, one control, and optionally a `sl:field-description` and a `sl:field-error`, in any order. Put `th:field` on the field, not on the control: the control takes it, gets the `id` the label points at (the field's name, `email`, also for a checkbox or switch), and an `aria-describedby` listing the description and, when the binding has errors, the error. The error shows the binding's messages. A field with errors gets `data-invalid`. Without `th:field`, set `for` to the control's id.

attributes.name: orientation
attributes.description: Stack the label above the control, or put them side by side (a checkbox or switch, then its label). `responsive` stacks them in a narrow `sl:field-group` and puts them side by side in a wide one.

attributes.name: for
attributes.description: The id of the control: for a field without `th:field`, or to use another id than the field's name. The control gets it when it has no id of its own, and the description and error ids derive from it.

elements.name: sl:field-content
elements.description: Stacks a `sl:field-label` with its `sl:field-description` or `sl:field-error`, beside the control of a horizontal `sl:field`.

elements.name: sl:field-description
elements.description: Help text for a `sl:field` or `sl:field-set`. It gets the id the control's (or fieldset's) `aria-describedby` points at.

elements.name: sl:field-error
elements.description: The error messages of a `sl:field` or `sl:field-set`, read from its `th:field`'s binding: one message as text, several as a list. It renders nothing while there are none. Content of its own replaces the messages, and always shows. It gets the id the control's (or fieldset's) `aria-describedby` points at while it shows messages.

elements.name: sl:field-group
elements.description: Stacks `sl:field`s and `sl:field-set`s with even spacing. Fields with `orientation="responsive"` inside it go side by side when it is wide enough.

elements.name: sl:field-label
elements.description: The label of a `sl:field`. Its `for` points at the field's control; a `for` of your own wins.

elements.name: sl:field-legend
elements.description: The caption of a `sl:field-set`, as its `legend`. Put it first in the fieldset.

attributes.name: variant
attributes.description: A section heading, or the size of a field label (for a set of options that answers one question).

elements.name: sl:field-set
elements.description: A group of related fields or options under a `sl:field-legend`, as a `fieldset`. With `th:field`, the options inside share it: radio buttons in a `sl:radio-group`, or checkboxes each in a `sl:field` of their own (which then need no `th:field` and get Spring's numbered ids, `toppings1`). A `sl:field-description` and `sl:field-error` directly inside describe the fieldset, and it gets `data-invalid` when the binding has errors.

elements.name: sl:file-upload
elements.description: A drop zone to pick files with, and the list of the files picked. Shadleaf's own: shadcn/ui has none. A visually hidden `<input type="file">` holds the files and is submitted with the form, so put `th:field` on the component (a `MultipartFile`, or with `multiple` a `List<MultipartFile>`) and give the form `enctype="multipart/form-data"`. Every attribute that is not a prop goes to the input (`th:field`, `name`, `id`, `required`, `disabled`, `aria-*`, `hx-*`); `class` is appended to the component. In a `sl:field`, the input takes the field's `th:field`, id and `aria-describedby`. With JavaScript, files can be dropped too, each picked file shows as an `sl:attachment` with a remove button, and a file that does not match `accept` or is larger than `max-size` shows as an error. Without it, the Browse button still picks files. The server checks the files anyway.

attributes.name: multiple
attributes.description: Take more than one file. Picking or dropping files adds them to the ones already there.

attributes.name: accept
attributes.description: The file types to take, as the input's `accept`: extensions (`.pdf`), MIME types (`application/pdf`) or `image/*`, separated by commas. A dropped file of another type is not added.

attributes.name: max-size
attributes.description: The largest file to take, as Spring Boot writes sizes: `10MB`, `500KB`. A larger file is not added.

attributes.name: level
attributes.description: Makes the title a heading of this level (`role="heading"`).

attributes.name: browse-label
attributes.description: The text of the Browse button. Defaults to "Browse files", or "Browse" without `multiple`.

elements.name: sl:form-errors
elements.description: The errors of the form object the enclosing `th:object` selects, shown as a destructive alert: by default the errors that belong to the whole form rather than one field (global errors, from `bindingResult.reject(...)` or a class-level constraint); with `show="all"` the field errors too. One message as text, several as a list. It renders nothing while there are none. Content of its own replaces the messages, and always shows. Not announced, and not focused unless it has `autofocus`; it has an id (`signup-errors` for `th:object="${signup}"`) and `tabindex="-1"`, so a link or a script can move focus to it too.

attributes.name: show
attributes.description: Which errors to list: the global errors only, or all of them, the global ones first and then every field's (each field keeps its own error too). Field messages are listed as they are, without the field's label, so write them to make sense on their own.

attributes.name: title
attributes.description: The title above the messages. Defaults to the message `sl.form-errors.title` ("There is a problem"); use `th:title` for a message of your own.

attributes.name: level
attributes.description: Heading level of the title. With it the title is a heading (`role="heading"` and `aria-level`) that screen reader users can jump to; without it, plain text.

attributes.name: autofocus
attributes.description: Move focus to the problem when the form comes back with errors: to the summary when it shows, otherwise to the first control with errors below it (in a field or with a `th:field` of its own). Nothing takes focus while the form has no errors. htmx honours it in swapped content too.

elements.name: sl:icon
elements.description: Inlines the SVG of an icon: the bundled lucide icons, or the application's own through an `IconSource` bean. An unknown name fails with the closest known ones.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: Name of the icon, e.g. `trash`. Lucide's names and aliases, plus any icons the application registers.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description: Width and height in pixels. Without it the icon is 24 pixels, or sized by the surrounding component (16 pixels inside a button).

attributes.name: stroke-width
attributes.description: Stroke width, overriding the icon's own (2 for lucide).

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Accessible name for an icon that carries meaning on its own. Without it the icon is decorative and hidden from assistive technology.

elements.name: sl:input
elements.description: A text input. Every attribute that is not a prop (`th:field`, `name`, `placeholder`, `required`, `hx-*`) passes through; `class` is appended to `input`. With `th:field`, the input is marked `aria-invalid` when its field has errors. In a `sl:field`, it takes the field's `th:field`, id and `aria-describedby`.

attributes.name: type
attributes.description: Type of the input. Checkboxes and radio buttons have components of their own.

elements.name: sl:input-group
elements.description: An input with text, icons or buttons inside its border: one `sl:input-group-input` or `sl:input-group-textarea`, and `sl:input-group-addon`s around it. Put the addons after the control in the markup, so the control comes first in the tab order and is read first; `align` on the addon places it. The group draws the control's focus ring, error and disabled look. In a `sl:field`, the control takes the field's `th:field`, id and `aria-describedby`.

elements.name: sl:input-group-addon
elements.description: Text, an icon, a `sl:kbd` or `sl:input-group-button`s beside or around the control of a `sl:input-group`. Clicking it, outside a button or link, focuses the control. Write it after the control: `align` places it.

attributes.name: align
attributes.description: Where the addon goes: before or after the control on its line, or above or below it across the whole group.

attributes.name: border
attributes.description: With `align` `block-start` or `block-end`, a dividing line between the addon and the control, with matching spacing.

elements.name: sl:input-group-button
elements.description: A button in a `sl:input-group-addon`: a `sl:button`, ghost and extra small by default, sized to fit inside the group. Any other attribute passes through to the `sl:button` (`type`, `loading`, `disabled`, `hx-*`). Requires `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` when `size` is `icon-xs` or `icon-sm`.

attributes.name: variant
attributes.description: Visual style of the button, as on `sl:button`.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description: Size of the button. The `icon` sizes are square, for a button that holds only an icon, and need an `aria-label`.

elements.name: sl:input-group-input
elements.description: The input of a `sl:input-group`: a `sl:input` without a border of its own, as the group draws it. Every attribute that is not a prop (`th:field`, `name`, `placeholder`, `required`, `hx-*`) passes through; `class` is appended to `input`. With `th:field`, the input is marked `aria-invalid` when its field has errors. In a `sl:field`, it takes the field's `th:field`, id and `aria-describedby`.

elements.name: sl:input-group-text
elements.description: Muted text in a `sl:input-group-addon`: a currency symbol, a unit, a domain. It may hold an `sl:icon`. In an addon above or below the control, it takes the free space, so what follows it sits at the end.

elements.name: sl:input-group-textarea
elements.description: The textarea of a `sl:input-group`: a `sl:textarea` without a border of its own, as the group draws it, that grows with its content where the browser supports it. Addons go above or below it (`align` `block-start` or `block-end`). The content is the initial text, unless `th:field` sets it. Every attribute that is not a prop passes through; `class` is appended to `textarea`. With `th:field`, the textarea is marked `aria-invalid` when its field has errors. In a `sl:field`, it takes the field's `th:field`, id and `aria-describedby`.

elements.name: sl:kbd
elements.description: A key on the keyboard, as text (`Ctrl`) or an `sl:icon`. Several keys pressed together go in an `sl:kbd-group`.

elements.name: sl:kbd-group
elements.description: A key combination: `sl:kbd` elements, with any text between them (such as `+`). HTML nests the keys of a combination in an outer `kbd`, as this does.

elements.name: sl:label
elements.description: A label for a form control. Point it at the control with `for` (the control's `id`; `th:field` gives the control an `id` equal to the field name), or put the control inside it.

elements.name: sl:month-view
elements.description: A month to look at, rendered on the server: each day shows content of its own (a badge, a short text, a count) from the `day` slot, which is rendered once per day and sees the day as `${slDay}` (`date`, a `LocalDate`, `iso`, `number`, `label`, `outside`, `today`), and can link to a page for that day. Nothing is picked: for a date in a form, use `sl:calendar`. The previous and next month are links to the same page with `?month=2026-09`, every other parameter kept, so it needs no JavaScript and works with htmx.

attributes.name: month
attributes.description: The month shown, as `2026-10` (a `YearMonth`) or a date in it. By default the month the request asks for in `month-param`, or else the current month.

attributes.name: month-param
attributes.description: The request parameter the links to the previous and next month set, and that gives the month when `month` is not set.

attributes.name: day-href
attributes.description: Makes every day a link: `{date}` is replaced by the day's ISO date (`/agenda/{date}`, `?date={date}`), and the result is a Thymeleaf link, so a path starting with `/` gets the context path. The `day` slot is then inside the link: put nothing interactive in it.

attributes.name: today
attributes.description: Today, as `2026-10-23` (a `LocalDate`), marked as the current date. By default the server's date; pass it in the user's time zone when that differs.

attributes.name: show-outside-days
attributes.description: Show the days of the previous and next month that fill the first and last week.

attributes.name: show-week-number
attributes.description: Show the week numbers, counted as the page's locale counts them (ISO weeks in most of Europe).

attributes.name: week-starts-on
attributes.description: The first day of the week: 0 is Sunday, 1 Monday, up to 6. By default the page's locale decides.

elements.name: sl:native-select
elements.description: The browser's own `select`, styled, with its `option` and `optgroup` elements as content. `th:field` marks the bound option. Every attribute that is not a prop passes through to the `select`, except `class`, which goes to the wrapper around it (for its width). With `th:field`, the select is marked `aria-invalid` when its field has errors. In a `sl:field`, it takes the field's `th:field`, id and `aria-describedby`.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description: Height of the select. It replaces HTML's `size` attribute, which turns a select into a list box.

elements.name: sl:pagination
elements.description: Links to the other pages of a list, in a `nav`. Given the Spring Data `Page` it shows (`th:page="${people}"`) and no content of its own, it renders them all: Previous, the first and the last page, the current page with `siblings` on each side, an ellipsis for the pages left out, and Next. Every link keeps the request's other parameters (sort, size, filters) and has a stable id, so htmx can give the focus back after a swap. A `Slice`, which does not know how many pages there are, gets Previous and Next only. Without Spring Data, pass `current` and `total` instead. With content of its own it is the frame for a hand-written pagination of `sl:pagination-content`, `-item`, `-link`, `-previous`, `-next` and `-ellipsis`, as in shadcn/ui.

attributes.name: current
attributes.description: Without a `page`: the page shown now, counting from 1.

attributes.name: total
attributes.description: Without a `page`: the number of pages.

attributes.name: siblings
attributes.description: How many pages to show on each side of the current one.

attributes.name: qualifier
attributes.description: The `@Qualifier` of the controller's `Pageable`, for a second list on the page: its links use `members_page` instead of `page`, and their ids start with `members-`.

attributes.name: th:page
attributes.description: The Spring Data `Page` or `Slice` shown now.

elements.name: sl:pagination-content
elements.description: The list (`ul`) of a hand-written `sl:pagination`, holding `sl:pagination-item`s.

elements.name: sl:pagination-ellipsis
elements.description: Stands for the pages a `sl:pagination` leaves out: an ellipsis, read as "More pages" (the message `sl.pagination.more`).

elements.name: sl:pagination-item
elements.description: One entry (`li`) of a `sl:pagination-content`: holds a link, Previous, Next or an ellipsis.

elements.name: sl:pagination-link
elements.description: A link to one page, drawn as a ghost button, or an outline one for the page shown now (`active`). Give it an `href` or `th:href`, and the page number as content.

attributes.name: active
attributes.description: Whether it is the page shown now: `aria-current="page"` and the outline look.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description: Size of the link, as on `sl:button`: square by default, for a number.

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description: There is nowhere to go: the link loses its `href`, gets `aria-disabled` and leaves the tab order, as a disabled `sl:button as="a"`.

elements.name: sl:pagination-next
elements.description: The link to the next page: a `sl:pagination-link` with a chevron and the text "Next" (the message `sl.pagination.next`), which content of its own replaces. Its name is "Go to next page" (`sl.pagination.next.label`); an `aria-label` replaces it. On a narrow screen only the chevron shows.

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description: There is no next page: the link loses its `href`, gets `aria-disabled` and leaves the tab order.

elements.name: sl:pagination-previous
elements.description: The link to the previous page: a `sl:pagination-link` with a chevron and the text "Previous" (the message `sl.pagination.previous`), which content of its own replaces. Its name is "Go to previous page" (`sl.pagination.previous.label`); an `aria-label` replaces it. On a narrow screen only the chevron shows.

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description: There is no previous page: the link loses its `href`, gets `aria-disabled` and leaves the tab order.

elements.name: sl:pagination-size
elements.description: "Rows per page" and a menu of page sizes, as in shadcn/ui's data table. The sizes are `sl:dropdown-menu-radio-item` links: each asks for the same request with that size, every other parameter kept except the page number, so the list starts on the first page. It works without JavaScript (the menu is a popover). Takes the Spring Data `Page` shown now, whose size is the checked one; a size the page has but `sizes` does not list is added. The label is the message `sl.pagination-size.label`. Attributes go to the wrapper.

attributes.name: sizes
attributes.description: The sizes to choose from, separated by commas.

attributes.name: qualifier
attributes.description: The `@Qualifier` of the controller's `Pageable`, for a second list on the page: its links use `members_size` instead of `size`.

attributes.name: id
attributes.description: The menu's id; its button gets `-trigger` added, its label `-label`. `page-size` when not set, prefixed with the qualifier (`members-page-size`).

attributes.name: th:page
attributes.description: The Spring Data `Page` or `Slice` shown now.

elements.name: sl:pagination-summary
elements.description: Where the page is in the results, as text: "11–20 of 270", or with `format="page"` "Page 2 of 27". Takes the Spring Data `Page` shown now (`th:page`); for a `Slice`, which does not know the total, "11–20" or "Page 2". The words are messages (`sl.pagination.summary*`), so an application rewords or translates them; numbers are formatted for the locale.

attributes.name: format
attributes.description: `range`: the rows shown and the total. `page`: the page number and the number of pages.

attributes.name: th:page
attributes.description: The Spring Data `Page` or `Slice` shown now.

elements.name: sl:popover
elements.description: Rich content in a panel that opens from a button, on the browser's Popover API: it sits above the page next to its trigger, and Escape, a click outside or moving the focus out of it closes it. Holds a `sl:popover-trigger` and a `sl:popover-content`. Renders no element of its own.

attributes.name: id
attributes.description: The popover's id, which the trigger points at with `popovertarget`. The title and description ids derive from it.

elements.name: sl:popover-content
elements.description: The panel of a `sl:popover`, next to its trigger in the top layer. It is a non-modal dialog: name it with a `sl:popover-title` (in a `sl:popover-header`) or an `aria-label`. When it opens, focus moves to its first control. It flips to the other side when there is no room.

attributes.name: side
attributes.description: The side of the trigger it opens on. `right` and `left` are the end and the start of a line: on a right-to-left page a `right` popover opens on the left.

attributes.name: align
attributes.description: How it lines up with the trigger along that side.

elements.name: sl:popover-description
elements.description: Supporting text below a `sl:popover-title`, which describes the popover (`aria-describedby`). Its id derives from the popover's (`dimensions-description`).

elements.name: sl:popover-header
elements.description: The top of a `sl:popover-content`, holding `sl:popover-title` and `sl:popover-description`.

elements.name: sl:popover-title
elements.description: The title of a `sl:popover`, inside `sl:popover-header`, which names the popover (`aria-labelledby`). Its id derives from the popover's (`dimensions-title`).

attributes.name: level
attributes.description: Heading level. With it the title is a heading (`role="heading"` and `aria-level`); without it, plain text, as in shadcn/ui.

elements.name: sl:popover-trigger
elements.description: The button that opens and closes a `sl:popover`: a `sl:button` with `popovertarget` set to the popover. Any other attribute passes through to the `sl:button`.

attributes.name: variant
attributes.description: Visual style of the button, as on `sl:button`.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description: Size of the button, as on `sl:button`. The `icon` sizes need an `aria-label`.

elements.name: sl:query-params
elements.description: Hidden inputs that copy the current request's query parameters into a `GET` form, so sending a search keeps the table's order, page size and other filters. Name the form's own fields in `except`, or they are sent twice. The page number is always left out, so a new search starts on the first page. Values are decoded once and escaped like any other attribute; a repeated parameter (several `sort` values) stays repeated. Renders no element of its own. Other attributes go to every input: `form="search"` ties them to a form elsewhere on the page.

attributes.name: except
attributes.description: The parameters not to copy, separated by commas: the fields the form has itself (`q`, `q,status`).

attributes.name: qualifier
attributes.description: The `@Qualifier` of the controller's `Pageable`, for a second table on the page: its page parameter (`members_page`) is the one left out.

elements.name: sl:radio-group
elements.description: A group of `sl:radio-group-item`s, announced as a radio group. Name it with `aria-labelledby` (pointing at the question) or `aria-label`. The items share their `name`, or their `th:field`, which is what makes them one choice.

attributes.name: orientation
attributes.description: Stack the items, or put them on a row that wraps.

elements.name: sl:radio-group-item
elements.description: One radio button in `sl:radio-group`: the browser's own, styled. Give it a `value` and the group's `name`, or `th:field` with a `value` or `th:value`; Spring then numbers the ids (`plan1`, `plan2`), so put the item inside its label. In a `sl:field-set` with `th:field`, the items take its field. Every attribute that is not a prop passes through; `class` is appended to `radio-group-item`. With `th:field`, the item is marked `aria-invalid` when its field has errors.

elements.name: sl:select
elements.description: A select drawn like shadcn/ui's: a real `select` with `sl:select-item`, `sl:select-group` and `sl:select-separator` as content, so `th:field`, submitting and the keyboard work as for any select. Where the browser supports the customizable select (`appearance: base-select`) it draws the list itself; elsewhere `slSelect` puts a list box in its place once Alpine runs. Every attribute that is not a prop passes through to the `select`, except `class`, which goes to the wrapper around it. In a `sl:field`, it takes the field's `th:field`, id and `aria-describedby`.

attributes.name: placeholder
attributes.description: Text shown while no option is chosen: a first option with an empty value, hidden from the list. A required select with it selected is invalid.

elements.name: sl:select-group
elements.description: A group of `sl:select-item`s under a heading: an `optgroup`.

elements.name: sl:select-item
elements.description: An option in a `sl:select`: an `option` with a check mark that shows while it is chosen. `value` (or `th:value`) and `disabled` pass through; `th:field` on the select marks the bound one. Its content may start with an icon; always give it text, which is all an older browser keeps of it.

elements.name: sl:select-separator
elements.description: A line between items or groups of a `sl:select`: an `hr`, which every current browser draws in a select's list.

elements.name: sl:separator
elements.description: A thin line between content. A vertical one stretches to the height of the row it is in, so it needs a flex container.

attributes.name: decorative
attributes.description: Hide the line from assistive technology, as most separators only draw a line. With `decorative="false"` it is announced as a separator, for one that divides content into groups.

elements.name: sl:sheet
elements.description: A dialog that slides in from an edge of the screen, for content that complements the page: filters, settings, details. Built on the native `dialog` element, like `sl:dialog`: the page behind it is inert, Escape and a click outside close it, and focus returns to where it came from. Build it from `sl:sheet-header` (holding `sl:sheet-title` and `sl:sheet-description`), your content and `sl:sheet-footer`. A button opens it with `commandfor` set to the sheet's `id` and `command="show-modal"`.

attributes.name: id
attributes.description: The sheet's id, which the buttons that open and close it point at with `commandfor`. The title and description ids derive from it.

attributes.name: side
attributes.description: The edge it slides in from. `right` and `left` are the end and the start of a line: on a right-to-left page a `right` sheet opens on the left.

attributes.name: open
attributes.description: Open the sheet as soon as it is on the page, for a sheet the server renders in answer to a request (an htmx swap). Needs Alpine.

attributes.name: show-close-button
attributes.description: A close button (an x) in the corner.

elements.name: sl:sheet-body
elements.description: The content of a `sl:sheet` between its header and footer, which scrolls by itself so the header and footer stay in view. Its content has the id `<id>-body` (`edit-body`), the target for htmx: a request from outside that targets it opens the sheet at once and shows a spinner until the answer is swapped in; closing aborts a request still running. Left empty, it is emptied again when the sheet closes, so it never shows the previous content. When a request fails, the error shows in the sheet, or, for the request that opened it, as a toast (see `load-error`). Needs Alpine.

attributes.name: load-error
attributes.description: What happens when the request that opened the sheet fails: `toast` closes it and shows the error as a toast (shown in the sheet when the page has no `sl:toaster`); `inline` keeps it open with the error in it. A failed request from inside (a form) always shows the error in the sheet, so nothing typed is lost.

elements.name: sl:sheet-description
elements.description: Supporting text below a `sl:sheet-title`, which describes the sheet (`aria-describedby`). Its id derives from the sheet's (`filters-description`).

elements.name: sl:sheet-footer
elements.description: The bottom of a `sl:sheet`, for its actions, stacked. It stays at the bottom of a sheet on the side of the screen however little content there is above it.

attributes.name: show-close-button
attributes.description: An outline "Close" button after the other actions.

elements.name: sl:sheet-header
elements.description: The top of a `sl:sheet`: a `sl:sheet-title` and an optional `sl:sheet-description` below it.

elements.name: sl:sheet-title
elements.description: The title of a `sl:sheet`, inside `sl:sheet-header`: a heading that names the sheet (`aria-labelledby`). Its id derives from the sheet's (`filters-title`).

attributes.name: level
attributes.description: Heading level (`role="heading"` and `aria-level`). A sheet starts an outline of its own, so the default, 2, rarely needs changing.

elements.name: sl:sidebar
elements.description: The application's navigation, inside `sl:sidebar-provider`. One element serves both widths: from 768 px up it is a column beside the page, which the trigger collapses and expands; below that it is a panel over the page, which the trigger opens. It is a `nav` named "Main" (`sl.sidebar.label`; an `aria-label` replaces it) and a popover: the browser opens the panel in the top layer and closes it on Escape or a click outside. On a phone, Alpine moves the focus into the open panel and makes the rest of the page inert, and closes it when a link in it is followed. It holds `sl:sidebar-header`, `sl:sidebar-content` (groups of menus) and `sl:sidebar-footer`. With `placement="header"` it goes inside `sl:site-header` instead, where from 768 px it is a row of links; on a phone it is the same panel.

attributes.name: id
attributes.description: The id the trigger points at (`sl:sidebar-trigger`'s `for`).

attributes.name: side
attributes.description: The edge it sits on, as on `sl:sheet`: `left` is the start of a line and `right` the end, so they swap on a right-to-left page.

attributes.name: placement
attributes.description: Where it sits on a desktop: `sidebar` is a column beside the page; `header` a row of links inside `sl:site-header` (the header layout), which never collapses: `collapsible`, the collapsed state and the trigger do not apply there (the trigger is hidden), and `side` only picks the phone panel's edge. Collapsible items and the parts marked `panel-only` are left out of the row; the phone panel is the same for both.

attributes.name: variant
attributes.description: How it looks on a desktop: `sidebar` is a column along the edge with a border; `floating` a panel with a margin all round; `inset` lays the sidebar's ground around the page, which (`sl:sidebar-inset`) becomes a card on it. The phone panel looks the same for all three. In the header placement only `inset` counts: the page becomes a card below the header.

attributes.name: collapsible
attributes.description: How it collapses on a desktop: `offcanvas` moves it out of view entirely; `icon` narrows it to a strip of its menu buttons' icons (labels, badges, actions and sub-menus hidden; a menu button's `tooltip` shows its label); `none` never collapses it, and the trigger is hidden on a desktop. The phone panel is the same for all three.

elements.name: sl:sidebar-content
elements.description: The part of the `sl:sidebar` that scrolls, between `sl:sidebar-header` and `sl:sidebar-footer`; it holds the `sl:sidebar-group`s. A plain `div`: the sidebar itself is the navigation landmark.

elements.name: sl:sidebar-footer
elements.description: The bottom of the `sl:sidebar`: settings, help or the signed-in user, below the `sl:sidebar-content`. It does not scroll with the content.

attributes.name: panel-only
attributes.description: Show it only in the phone panel: from 768 px it is left out (`display: none`), so a header row or a sidebar stays short.

elements.name: sl:sidebar-group
elements.description: A section of the `sl:sidebar`'s links: an optional `sl:sidebar-group-label` and `sl:sidebar-group-action`, then `sl:sidebar-group-content` with a `sl:sidebar-menu`. With a label it is a group named by that label (`role="group"`, `aria-labelledby`), so a screen reader says "Platform, group" when the focus moves into it; without one it is a plain `div`.

attributes.name: id
attributes.description: The group's id. Its label gets `<id>-label`; without an id, each render generates one (`sl-sidebar-group-` and eight random characters).

attributes.name: panel-only
attributes.description: Show it only in the phone panel: from 768 px it is left out (`display: none`), so a header row or a sidebar stays short.

attributes.name: collapsible
attributes.description: Make it a section that opens and closes, on the browser's `details` element: its `sl:sidebar-group-label` (which must come first) becomes the `summary`, with a chevron at the end. Collapsed to icons, and in the header row, its links show whether it is open or not.

attributes.name: open
attributes.description: Render a collapsible group open, for instance when it holds the current page: `th:open="${#slNav.current('/build')}"`.

attributes.name: icon-hidden
attributes.description: Leave the group out while the sidebar is collapsed to icons (`collapsible="icon"`), as for a group whose links have no icons of their own. Expanded, and in the phone panel, it shows as usual.

elements.name: sl:sidebar-group-action
elements.description: An icon button at the end of a `sl:sidebar-group`'s label, such as "Add project". It holds only an icon, so it needs an `aria-label`. Every other attribute passes through (`hx-*`, `commandfor`, `href`). Requires `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.

attributes.name: as
attributes.description: Element to render: a `button`, or an anchor (`a`) to a page.

attributes.name: type
attributes.description: Submit behaviour of the button; defaults to `button`.

elements.name: sl:sidebar-group-content
elements.description: The content of a `sl:sidebar-group`, below its label: usually one `sl:sidebar-menu`.

elements.name: sl:sidebar-group-label
elements.description: The name of a `sl:sidebar-group`, in small muted text above its menu.
