The group is labelled by it, so it gets an id from the group (`<group id>-label`); give the group an `id` rather than the label. In a `collapsible` group it is the `summary` that opens and closes it, with a chevron at the end, and must be the group's first part.

elements.name: sl:sidebar-header
elements.description: The top of the `sl:sidebar`: the application or team, above the `sl:sidebar-content`. It does not scroll with the content.

attributes.name: panel-only
attributes.description: Show it only in the phone panel: from 768 px it is left out (`display: none`), so a header row or a sidebar stays short.

elements.name: sl:sidebar-inset
elements.description: The page's main content beside the `sl:sidebar`: the `main` element, which takes the rest of the width. Put the page header with the `sl:sidebar-trigger` at its top. It is the target of a `sl:skip-link`: `tabindex="-1"` lets the link move the focus to it.

attributes.name: id
attributes.description: The element's id, which a `sl:skip-link` points at (`main` is its default too).

elements.name: sl:sidebar-menu
elements.description: A list of links (or buttons) in the `sl:sidebar`: a `ul` of `sl:sidebar-menu-item`s, so a screen reader says how many there are.

elements.name: sl:sidebar-menu-action
elements.description: An icon button at the end of a `sl:sidebar-menu-item`, beside its `sl:sidebar-menu-button`: a second action for that entry, such as "More" or "Remove from favourites". It holds only an icon, so it needs an `aria-label` that names the entry too ("More for Design Engineering"). Every other attribute passes through. Requires `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.

attributes.name: as
attributes.description: Element to render: a `button`, or an anchor (`a`) to a page.

attributes.name: type
attributes.description: Submit behaviour of the button; defaults to `button`.

attributes.name: show-on-hover
attributes.description: From 768 px, show it only while the pointer is over the item, the focus is in it, or its menu is open (`aria-expanded="true"`). Always shown on a phone.

elements.name: sl:sidebar-menu-badge
elements.description: A count at the end of a `sl:sidebar-menu-button`, inside the same `sl:sidebar-menu-item`. The button is described by it, so a screen reader says the count after the link's name ("Inbox, link, 12"); the badge gets its id from the item (`<item id>-badge`). Clicks go through it to the button.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: What a screen reader says instead of the visible text, such as "12 unread messages". The visible count is then hidden from it.

elements.name: sl:sidebar-menu-button
elements.description: A link (or button) in a `sl:sidebar-menu-item`: an icon in the `icon-start` slot, then the label. Mark the current page with `active`, for instance `th:active="${#slNav.current('/people')}"`. The label is cut off with an ellipsis when it does not fit; for two lines, put each in an element of its own (`<strong>`, `<small>`). Every attribute that is not a prop passes through (`href`, `hx-*`); `class` is appended to `sidebar-menu-button`. In a `collapsible` `sl:sidebar-menu-item` it is the item's `summary`, which opens and closes the group, with a chevron at the end; `as`, `type` and `disabled` do not apply there, and it takes no `href`.

attributes.name: as
attributes.description: Element to render: an anchor (`a`) to a page, or a `button` for an action.

attributes.name: active
attributes.description: The current one: the link gets `aria-current="page"`, a button `aria-current="true"`, and both the active look.

attributes.name: variant
attributes.description: Visual style: `outline` adds a background and a border.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description: Height: `sm` for a dense list, `lg` for an entry with two lines, such as the application's name in the `sl:sidebar-header`.

attributes.name: type
attributes.description: Submit behaviour of a button; defaults to `button`.

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description: Disable it. A disabled link loses its `href` and leaves the tab order.

attributes.name: tooltip
attributes.description: The label to show beside the button while the sidebar is collapsed to icons (`collapsible="icon"`), on hover and on keyboard focus; usually the same words as the label. Not shown while the sidebar is expanded or on a phone. It repeats the button's name, so it is hidden from assistive technology and describes nothing (`sl:tooltip`'s `mode="label"`).

elements.name: sl:sidebar-menu-item
elements.description: One entry of a `sl:sidebar-menu`: an `li` holding a `sl:sidebar-menu-button`, and optionally a `sl:sidebar-menu-badge` or a `sl:sidebar-menu-action` beside it. With a badge, the button is described by it (`aria-describedby`), so a screen reader says "Inbox, link, 12". With `collapsible` it is a group of links that opens and closes: the menu button is what the user clicks, followed by a `sl:sidebar-menu-sub`.

attributes.name: id
attributes.description: The item's id. Its badge gets `<id>-badge`; without an id, each render generates one (`sl-sidebar-menu-item-` and eight random characters).

attributes.name: collapsible
attributes.description: Make it a group that opens and closes, on the browser's `details` element (no JavaScript needed): its `sl:sidebar-menu-button` becomes the `summary`, with a chevron, and its `sl:sidebar-menu-sub` the content. Collapsed to icons, a click on the button expands the sidebar and opens the group. It takes no badge or action: the browser would hide them with the sub-menu.

attributes.name: open
attributes.description: Render a collapsible item open, for instance when it holds the current page: `th:open="${#slNav.current('/settings')}"`.

attributes.name: panel-only
attributes.description: Show it only in the phone panel: from 768 px it is left out (`display: none`), so a header row or a sidebar stays short.

elements.name: sl:sidebar-menu-sub
elements.description: A list of links below a `sl:sidebar-menu-button`, indented along a line: a `ul` of `sl:sidebar-menu-sub-item`s. In a `collapsible` `sl:sidebar-menu-item` it is what opens and closes. With `collapsible` of its own it opens and closes by a chevron beside the menu button, which stays a link to a page of its own. Hidden while the sidebar is collapsed to icons. Requires `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` when `collapsible` is `true`.

attributes.name: collapsible
attributes.description: Open and close it with a chevron at the end of the menu button (a `summary`, drawn as a `sl:sidebar-menu-action`), so the menu button stays a link. The chevron holds only an icon, so it needs an `aria-label` that names the sub-menu ("Playground's pages"); every other attribute goes to the `ul`.

attributes.name: open
attributes.description: Render a collapsible sub-menu open, for instance when it holds the current page: `th:open="${#slNav.current('/playground')}"`.

elements.name: sl:sidebar-menu-sub-button
elements.description: A link (or button) in a `sl:sidebar-menu-sub-item`. Mark the current page with `active`, for instance `th:active="${#slNav.current('/settings/billing')}"`. An optional icon goes in the `icon-start` slot; the label is cut off with an ellipsis when it does not fit. Every attribute that is not a prop passes through (`href`, `hx-*`); `class` is appended to `sidebar-menu-sub-button`.

attributes.name: as
attributes.description: Element to render: an anchor (`a`) to a page, or a `button` for an action.

attributes.name: active
attributes.description: The current one: the link gets `aria-current="page"`, a button `aria-current="true"`, and both the active look.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description: Text size: `sm` for a denser list.

attributes.name: type
attributes.description: Submit behaviour of a button; defaults to `button`.

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description: Disable it. A disabled link loses its `href` and leaves the tab order.

elements.name: sl:sidebar-menu-sub-item
elements.description: One entry of a `sl:sidebar-menu-sub`: an `li` holding a `sl:sidebar-menu-sub-button`.

elements.name: sl:sidebar-provider
elements.description: The wrapper of an application shell with a sidebar: it holds `sl:sidebar`, and `sl:sidebar-inset` with the page's content (and the `sl:sidebar-trigger`), and it holds whether the sidebar is expanded or collapsed on a desktop. The server renders that state from the `sl-sidebar-state` cookie, which the browser writes when the user collapses or expands the sidebar (the trigger, or Ctrl/⌘+B), so every page starts in it without a jump. Below 768 px the sidebar is a panel the trigger opens instead, and the state does not apply. Needs Alpine for the trigger and the shortcut; without JavaScript the sidebar stays as the server rendered it.

attributes.name: state
attributes.description: The state to render, whatever the cookie says: for an application that keeps the choice itself, such as in the user's settings. Without it, the cookie decides.

attributes.name: default-state
attributes.description: The state before the user chose one (no cookie yet).

elements.name: sl:sidebar-separator
elements.description: A line between parts of the `sl:sidebar`, in the sidebar's border colour. Decorative: screen readers skip it.

elements.name: sl:sidebar-trigger
elements.description: The icon button that collapses and expands the `sl:sidebar` on a desktop and opens its panel on a phone. Named "Toggle sidebar" (`sl.sidebar.trigger`; an `aria-label` replaces it); content of its own replaces the icon. Without JavaScript it is hidden on a desktop, where it could not do anything, and still opens the panel on a phone. Any other attribute passes through to the `sl:button`.

attributes.name: for
attributes.description: The `id` of the sidebar it toggles.

attributes.name: variant
attributes.description: Visual style of the button, as on `sl:button`.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description: Size of the button: one of `sl:button`'s icon sizes.

elements.name: sl:site-header
elements.description: A header bar: a `header` laying out its content in a row. Across the top of the page (inside `sl:sidebar-provider`, before `sl:sidebar-inset`) it is the header layout's: a `sl:sidebar-trigger` that opens the menu on a phone, the application's name, the `sl:sidebar` with `placement="header"` as a row of links, and the `end` slot. At the top of `sl:sidebar-inset` it is the page's header in the sidebar layout: the trigger, a vertical `sl:separator` and a `sl:breadcrumb`. The `end` slot (search, the theme toggle, the signed-in user) goes to the end of the row.

elements.name: sl:skeleton
elements.description: A placeholder that pulses while content loads. It is hidden from assistive technology; mark the region that is loading with `aria-busy="true"` instead. Give it the size of what it stands in for with a class of your own.

attributes.name: shape
attributes.description: A line of text (full width, one line high) or a circle (an avatar).

elements.name: sl:skip-link
elements.description: A link past the navigation to the page's content, for keyboard users: put it first in the body. Hidden until it has the focus (the first Tab on the page), then drawn at the top of the page. Its text is "Skip to main content" (the message `sl.skip-link`), which content of its own replaces. The target should be able to take the focus: `sl:sidebar-inset` is `id="main"` with `tabindex="-1"`, so the default target works with it.

attributes.name: for
attributes.description: The `id` of the element it skips to, usually the `main`.

elements.name: sl:spinner
elements.description: A spinning icon that says something is loading: a status (`role="status"`) named "Loading" (the message `sl.spinner.label`; an `aria-label` of its own replaces it). It turns slower, not still, when the user asks for reduced motion. For a button that is busy, use `sl:button loading` instead.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description: Width and height in pixels. Without it the spinner is 16 pixels, or sized by the surrounding component (as an icon in `sl:empty-media`).

elements.name: sl:switch
elements.description: A switch: a checkbox with `role="switch"`, announced as on or off. It submits like a checkbox, so `th:field` on a boolean works as it does there (numbered id, hidden marker input; in a `sl:field`, the field's name as id). Every attribute that is not a prop passes through; `class` is appended to `switch`. With `th:field`, the switch is marked `aria-invalid` when its field has errors.

elements.name: sl:table
elements.description: A table in shadcn/ui's look. Write the plain table elements inside it (`caption`, `thead`, `tbody`, `tfoot`, `tr`, `th`, `td`), with `th:each` on a row; there is no component per row or cell. Use `sl:table-head` for a header cell that sorts or aligns, and `sl:table-empty` for the row that says nothing was found. The table scrolls sideways inside its own container when it is wider than the page. Attributes go to the `table`.

attributes.name: qualifier
attributes.description: The `@Qualifier` of the controller's `Pageable`, for a second table on the page: its sort links use `members_sort` instead of `sort`.

attributes.name: th:page
attributes.description: The Spring Data `Page` or `Slice` the table shows. Its `Sort` tells every `sl:table-head` inside how the rows are sorted now. Without it, the headers read the order from the request's sort parameter.

elements.name: sl:table-empty
elements.description: The row a `sl:table` shows when there are no rows to show: one cell across every column saying "No results." (the message `sl.table.empty`). Content of its own replaces the text. Render it with `th:if`, e.g. `th:if="${people.empty}"`.

attributes.name: colspan
attributes.description: The number of columns the cell spans: all of the table's.

elements.name: sl:table-head
elements.description: A header cell (`th`) of a `sl:table`. With `sort` its label is a link that sorts the table by that property on the server: ascending, or descending when it is sorted ascending already. The link keeps the request's other parameters (filters, page size) and goes back to the first page. The sorted column gets `aria-sort` and an arrow. A plain `th` works too, for a header that does neither.

attributes.name: sort
attributes.description: The property to sort by, as the controller's `Sort` names it (`name`, `address.city`). Only the first key of the current order is shown.

attributes.name: align
attributes.description: Where the label sits in the cell. Put the same `data-align` on the column's `td`s: `end` for amounts.

elements.name: sl:table-select-all
elements.description: A checkbox for a header cell of a `sl:table` that selects every row on the page. The rows are the application's own checkboxes (a `sl:checkbox` with `name="ids"` and `th:value="${person.id}"`) in the cells of the table's body; they submit without JavaScript. This one is checked when every row is, indeterminate when some are, and checks or unchecks them all when clicked; it is named "Select all rows on this page" (the message `sl.table.select-all`) unless it gets an `aria-label`. It needs JavaScript, so it stays hidden until Alpine starts. It fires `sl-table-selection-change` on the table (`{selected, total}`), which `sl:table-selection-count` shows. It submits nothing itself (no `name`); other attributes go to its `input`, `class` to its wrapper.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: The `name` of the row checkboxes, when the body has checkboxes of another kind too. Without it, every checkbox in a body cell is a row.

elements.name: sl:table-selection-count
elements.description: How many rows of a `sl:table` are selected: "2 of 20 selected" (the message `sl.table.selection.count`), kept up to date in the browser as rows are checked, as rows are replaced (an htmx swap) and after a form reset. Place it anywhere, e.g. at the start of the table's footer as shadcn/ui's data table does. It is not a live region: a click on `sl:table-select-all` announces the count, a row's checkbox announces its own state. Empty and hidden until Alpine starts.

attributes.name: for
attributes.description: The `id` of the table whose rows it counts (`sl:table` puts its `id` on the `table`).

elements.name: sl:tabs
elements.description: Panels of content shown one at a time, chosen from a row of tabs. Holds a `sl:tabs-list` of `sl:tabs-trigger`s and a `sl:tabs-content` per tab. The server renders the active tab's panel and hides the others, so the page is right before any script runs; Alpine adds switching in the browser and the keyboard (the ARIA tabs pattern). Give the triggers an `href` and the tabs work without JavaScript too.

attributes.name: id
attributes.description: The id of the tabs. The ids of the triggers and panels derive from it (`settings-account-trigger`, `settings-account-content`).

attributes.name: active
attributes.description: The `tab` of the trigger and panel that are active when the page renders, e.g. from a request parameter: `th:active="${tab}"`.

attributes.name: orientation
attributes.description: `vertical` puts the tabs in a column next to the panels, and the up and down arrow keys move between them.

attributes.name: activation-mode
attributes.description: `automatic`: a tab shows its panel as soon as the arrow keys reach it. `manual`: the arrow keys only move the focus, and Enter or Space shows the panel; for panels that are slow to show, such as ones loaded with htmx.

elements.name: sl:tabs-content
elements.description: The panel of one tab of a `sl:tabs`, labelled by its trigger. Only the active tab's panel shows; the others are `hidden`. It takes the focus with Tab after the tabs (as in Radix), so a panel without controls can be read and scrolled.

attributes.name: tab
attributes.description: Which tab's panel this is: the `tab` of its `sl:tabs-trigger`.

elements.name: sl:tabs-list
elements.description: The row (or column) of `sl:tabs-trigger`s of a `sl:tabs`: a `tablist`. An `aria-label` names it when the page has more than one.

attributes.name: variant
attributes.description: `default`: the tabs sit on a muted track and the active one is raised. `line`: no track, a line under the active tab.

elements.name: sl:tabs-trigger
elements.description: A tab in a `sl:tabs-list`, which shows the `sl:tabs-content` with the same `tab`. A button, or with an `href` a link to the page with this tab active: without JavaScript the link loads it, with Alpine the tab switches in place and the address follows.

attributes.name: tab
attributes.description: Which tab this is: the `tab` of its `sl:tabs-content`, and the value `sl:tabs`' `active` names. Part of the ids, so letters, digits and dashes.

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description: The tab cannot be chosen; the arrow keys skip it. A disabled link loses its `href`.

elements.name: sl:textarea
elements.description: A multi-line text input that grows with its content where the browser supports it. The content is the initial text, unless `th:field` sets it. Every attribute that is not a prop passes through; `class` is appended to `textarea`. With `th:field`, the textarea is marked `aria-invalid` when its field has errors. In a `sl:field`, it takes the field's `th:field`, id and `aria-describedby`.

elements.name: sl:theme-toggle
elements.description: Switches the page between the light and the dark theme, and remembers the choice in the browser under the key the theme script (`sl/layout :: theme-script`) reads before the first paint, so the next page starts in it. By default an icon button opening a menu with Light, Dark and System; with `as="button"` one button that switches between light and dark. Its icon shows the theme the page is in. Needs Alpine; without JavaScript it is not shown. Every attribute that is not a prop passes through to the button.

attributes.name: as
attributes.description: `menu`: a menu with Light, Dark and System (`menuitemradio`s). `button`: one toggle button for dark mode (`aria-pressed`), which cannot go back to following the system.

attributes.name: id
attributes.description: The menu's id (its button gets the id with `-trigger` added). Two menus on a page need different ids. With `as="button"` it is the button's id, rendered only when set.

attributes.name: variant
attributes.description: Visual style of the button, as on `sl:button`.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description: Size of the button: one of `sl:button`'s icon sizes.

attributes.name: side
attributes.description: The side of the button the menu opens on, as on `sl:dropdown-menu-content`.

attributes.name: align
attributes.description: How the menu lines up with the button along that side, as on `sl:dropdown-menu-content`: `end` lines up the end edges.

elements.name: sl:toast
elements.description: One toast in a `sl:toaster`: a title, an optional description and a close button. The server renders it for a message that has to show when the page loads, such as a flash attribute after a redirect, or in an out-of-band swap. Content of its own replaces the description. A toast goes away by itself, so it must never hold the only way to do something.

attributes.name: title
attributes.description: What happened, in a few words: "Member deleted".

attributes.name: description
attributes.description: More about it, under the title.

attributes.name: variant
attributes.description: The kind of message, shown by its icon: none, a check, an i, a warning triangle or an x. A screen reader announces an `error` at once, interrupting what it reads; the others when it is done.

attributes.name: duration
attributes.description: How long this toast shows, in milliseconds, instead of the toaster's `duration`. `0` keeps it until it is closed.

elements.name: sl:toaster
elements.description: Where toasts show: short messages in a corner of the page that close themselves, such as "Member deleted". Put one at the end of the layout's `body`. Toasts get there three ways: as `sl:toast`s inside it, which the server renders (e.g. from a flash attribute after a redirect); from an `sl-toast` event, which an htmx response sends with the `HX-Trigger` header; or swapped in out of band. A screen reader announces each toast, and toasts show above an open modal dialog and can be used there. Needs Alpine.

attributes.name: id
attributes.description: The toaster's id, which an out-of-band swap targets (`hx-swap-oob="beforeend:#toaster"`).

attributes.name: position
attributes.description: The corner or edge the toasts show in. `right` and `left` are the end and the start of a line.

attributes.name: duration
attributes.description: How long a toast shows, in milliseconds, unless it sets its own. The time stops while the pointer is on the toasts, while one of them has the focus and while the page is hidden. `0` keeps toasts until they are closed.

attributes.name: visible-toasts
attributes.description: How many toasts show at once, the newest ones. Older ones wait, with their time stopped, and show again when a newer one closes.

elements.name: sl:toggle
elements.description: A button that is on or off: a checkbox drawn as a button, so it submits, binds and works as one without JavaScript, and a screen reader announces it as checked or not. The content (text, icons) is its label; give a toggle that holds only an icon an `aria-label`. Every attribute that is not a prop (`th:field`, `name`, `value`, `checked`, `disabled`, `aria-label`, `x-*`) passes through to the `input`, except `class`, which goes to the `label` around it. `th:field` on a boolean works as on a checkbox; the toggle is marked `aria-invalid` when its field has errors.

elements.name: sl:toggle-group
elements.description: A row of `sl:toggle-group-item`s, of which one (`type="single"`, radio buttons) or several (`type="multiple"`, checkboxes) can be on. The items submit, bind and work as those inputs, without JavaScript. Name the group with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. Give it the `th:field` (or the `name`) its items share, or put it in a `sl:field-set` with `th:field`; each item then only needs a `value`. Every other attribute that is not a prop passes through to the group.

attributes.name: type
attributes.description: `single`: one item is on at a time, as radio buttons (the arrow keys move between them). `multiple`: any number, as checkboxes.

attributes.name: spacing
attributes.description: The gap between the items, in Tailwind's spacing steps (`2` is `0.5rem`). `0` joins them into one control.

attributes.name: orientation
attributes.description: Put the items on a row, or in a column.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: The `name` every item submits under, for a group without `th:field`. A `single` group without either gets a generated one, so its items still exclude each other.

elements.name: sl:toggle-group-item
elements.description: One item of a `sl:toggle-group`, drawn as a `sl:toggle`: a radio button in a `single` group, a checkbox in a `multiple` one. Give it a `value`; it takes the group's `th:field` or `name`, variant, size and `disabled`. The content is its label; give an item that holds only an icon an `aria-label`. Every attribute that is not a prop (`value`, `checked`, `disabled`, `aria-label`) passes through to the `input`, except `class`, which goes to the `label` around it. With `th:field`, the item is marked `aria-invalid` when its field has errors.

elements.name: sl:tooltip
elements.description: A short text that shows while the pointer rests on an element or the keyboard focuses it, on the browser's Popover API. The first element inside is the trigger, any focusable element (a `sl:button`, a link); the `sl:tooltip-content` after it describes it (`aria-describedby`). Escape hides it. Needs Alpine.

attributes.name: mode
attributes.description: What the text is to a screen reader: `description` adds it to the trigger as a description; `label` is for a text that repeats the trigger's name, such as an icon button's `aria-label`: it is hidden from assistive technology and describes nothing, so the name is not said twice.

attributes.name: delay
attributes.description: How long the pointer rests on the trigger before the tooltip shows, in milliseconds. Keyboard focus shows it at once, and so does moving to another trigger right after a tooltip hid.

elements.name: sl:tooltip-content
elements.description: The text of a `sl:tooltip` (`role="tooltip"`), after its trigger. Keep it short and plain: it cannot hold links or buttons, and touch screens never show it. It flips to the other side when there is no room. In a tooltip with `mode="label"` it is hidden from assistive technology (`aria-hidden`).

attributes.name: side
attributes.description: The side of the trigger it shows on. `right` and `left` are the end and the start of a line.

attributes.name: align
attributes.description: How it lines up with the trigger along that side.

elements.name: sl:user-menu
elements.description: The signed-in user (`#slUser.current`) with a menu that signs out, or a Sign in link for an anonymous visitor. In the sidebar's footer a large menu button with the user's picture, name and email (or username, when it is not the name); in the site header a button with the picture alone. Both open a `sl:dropdown-menu`: the user's name and email, the items in its content (Account, Settings), and Sign out, which posts to `#slUser.logoutUrl` (`shadleaf.security.logout-url`) from a form of its own, so `th:action` adds Spring Security's CSRF token. The picture goes through `sl:avatar`: while it loads, without one and when it fails to load, the initials show. Every attribute that is not a prop passes through to the button (or the Sign in link), except an `aria-label`, which only names the header's button: in the sidebar the button's name is the text it shows, and Sign in is named by its text.

attributes.name: placement
attributes.description: `sidebar`: a `sl:sidebar-menu` with one large menu button, for the `sl:sidebar-footer` (shadcn's NavUser). `header`: a round button with the picture, for the `end` slot of `sl:site-header`, named "Account: " and the user's name.

attributes.name: id
attributes.description: The menu's id. Its button gets the id with `-trigger` added, the sign-out form with `-sign-out`. Two user menus on a page need different ids.

attributes.name: side
attributes.description: The side of the button the menu opens on, as on `sl:dropdown-menu-content`. By default `right` in the sidebar (below the button in the phone panel) and `bottom` in the header.

attributes.name: align
attributes.description: How the menu lines up with the button along that side, as on `sl:dropdown-menu-content`.
